items.title: Photonic half-semimetals with dual semimetal-insulator topology
items.summary: Abstract Topological wave systems have largely evolved along two distinct paradigms: gapless topological semimetals and gapped topological insulators. While topological semimetals support bulk transport, they generally lack intrinsic selectivity among propagation channels; topological insulators enable robust transport but confine it to narrow interfaces, limiting spatial utilization. Here, we theoretically demonstrate and experimentally realize time-reversal-invariant spin-valley photonic half-semimetals (HSMs), which exhibit a dual semimetal-insulator topology within a single bulk band structure. In HSMs, the bandgap closes selectively in spin-valley space: for a given spin (valley), one valley (spin) is semimetallic while the other remains insulating. This coexistence of spin- and valley-resolved gapless and gapped band structures makes HSMs fundamentally distinct from both conventional semimetals and insulators. As a defining bulk phenomenon, an HSM functions as a spin-valley-locked beam splitter, intrinsically enabling valley-selective spin routing. Moreover, when four complementary HSMs are assembled into a periodic superlattice, the same dual topology enables reciprocal spin-valley-resolved multilane helical transport with 100% spatial utilization. These results establish HSMs as a platform for selective bulk wave control and multichannel topological transport beyond conventional topological phases.

items.title: Unified structural origin of functionality in spiral skyrmions revealed by 3D electron tomography
items.summary: Abstract Ferroelectric skyrmions exhibit a range of emergent phenomena, including collective dynamics, negative capacitance, and a strong electric-field-induced second-harmonic generation response. However, three-dimensional (3D) atomic-scale configurations of skyrmions are unclarified yet, making the relationship between the physical functionalities and their underlying structural origin remains elusive. Here, using atomic-scale electron tomography, we experimentally resolve the 3D structure of polar skyrmion for the first time in PbTiO 3 /SrTiO 3 superlattice. On the basis of large-data image acquisition with more than 95,000 3D coordinates of atoms, we visualize that the core of the skyrmions exhibit an upward spiraling morphology. By quantitatively analyzing the ferroelectric polarization and lattice distortion, we uncover an unconventional decoupling between the two at the skyrmion wall, where the polarization is suppressed, accompanied by a local enhancement of tetragonality exceeding 5% at the center of the wall. This increased tetragonality modifies the local free-energy landscape, enhancing the negative-capacitance response and field sensitivity at the skyrmion wall. The polar skyrmion wall hosts a concentration of emergent physical properties, thereby providing a unified structural origin for the functionalities and physical behaviors of skyrmions. This work establishes a real space basis for understanding the physical properties of polar skyrmions.

items.title: How does the brain do more with less energy?
Evidence of large-scale and room-temperature stair-stepped quantum spin Hall states in Bi4Br4
items.summary: Abstract Topological insulators host exotic quantum phenomena such as the quantum spin Hall (QSH) effect, which enables dissipationless one-dimensional edge conduction. Realizing such states at room temperature and on a macroscopic scale is essential for energy-efficient electronics and quantum technologies, yet remains a fundamental challenge due to material limitations. Here, using microwave impedance microscopy, we directly visualize robust conductive channels persisting up to 300 K in α -Bi 4 Br 4 nanowires. Their stability and scalability are likely enabled by a “stair-stepped” stacking configuration on the side facets, a multilayer geometry in which QSH edge states from individual layers remain spatially decoupled. This configuration circumvents the stringent alignment and layer-number constraints of previous proposals, allowing robust stair-stepped QSH (SS-QSH) conduction in structures several micrometers long and hundreds of nanometers high. Magnetic-field- and temperature-dependent measurements are consistent with the topological nature of these conductive channels, as further supported by our theoretical analysis. Crucially, the conductance peaks and bulk signals scale with nanowire height, verifying the stair-stepped origin. Our results are also successfully reproduced by finite-element analysis simulations. This work establishes α -Bi 4 Br 4 as a practical platform for high-temperature topological electronics and demonstrates a generalizable stacking strategy for designing scalable QSH systems.

items.title: Robust quasi-bound states in the continuum in bilayer terahertz metasurface with S4 point-group symmetry
items.summary: Abstract Metasurface-based bound states in the continuum (BICs) enable exceptional spatiotemporal control of light and substantially enhance light–matter interactions, making them highly attractive for applications in sensing, nonlinear optics, and integrated photonics. However, conventional BICs in single-layer metasurfaces rely on in-plane symmetry and are highly susceptible to structural perturbations, offering limited design flexibility and constraining both their robustness and functional diversity. To overcome these limitations, we theoretically propose and experimentally demonstrate a new class of symmetry-protected quasi-BICs in bilayer terahertz metasurfaces. These states are realized by coupling in-plane rotational and out-of-plane reflective symmetries through S 4 point-group operations. Moreover, we show that such QBICs exhibit strong robustness against structural defects and fabrication imperfections. This work overcomes the robustness limitations of conventional single-layer metasurface BICs and establishes a general design paradigm for photonic devices that harness BICs with enhanced stability and scalability.

items.title: Deciphering Critical Transition for AKI Deterioration by STIfuse: Fusing Dynamic and Static Representations
items.summary: Abstract Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a life-threatening condition with notably high in-hospital mortality, characterized by a three-phase progression: a relatively stable state (without imminent life threat), a critical pre-deterioration state (the time window which may be identified and in which timely intervention could prevent upcoming irreversible deterioration), and a deteriorated state (severe conditions such as death or rescue events). Accurate early prediction of AKI deterioration and deciphering the critical transition remain challenging because of complex, high-dimensional, noisy, and incomplete clinical data, as well as limited mechanistic understanding of disease progression. To solve this problem, we propose STIfuse (Spatiotemporal Information fusion), a unique dual-view framework that integrates deep learning (DL) and spatiotemporal information transformation (STI) based on Takens’ embedding theorem and critical slowing down (CSD) theory. The DL backbone encodes multi-dimensional static representations to capture structural dependencies, while the STI branch transforms high-dimensional spatial information into a low-dimensional dynamic representation. These views are fused by a multivariate Gaussian distribution: the means capture statistical levels for diagnosis, and the covariances reflect collective physiological fluctuations for early deterioration prediction. An optimal-transport-distance-based contrastive loss is employed to learn discriminative dynamic features between ˈcriticalˈ and ˈstableˈ states. Pretrained on the MIMIC-IV dataset and validated on five external cohorts (including MIMIC-III (with two independent cohorts), eICU, HiRID, and NWICU), STIfuse demonstrated superior performance in predicting 72-hour deterioration. Further analysis of single-cell multi-omics data study uncovered inflammatory cascades linking comorbidities to AKI. STIfuse provides an interpretable, robust and scalable framework for early warning of AKI deterioration prediction, highlighting its potential in utility and scalability for clinical foundation models.
